Below is the full 12-week programme summary for your 42‑year‑old male client (desk worker) with an L4–L5 herniation history (now asymptomatic). It integrates strength training, progressive Phase 2 intensity increases, two weekly cardio sessions, a spine‑safe core protocol, anti‑inflammatory nutrition guidance, 1RM testing in Week 12 (trap‑bar deadlift and barbell hip thrust recommended), and a sleep & recovery protocol. All exercises are selected to avoid heavy axial spinal compression and loaded spinal flexion; if anything causes pain, stop and consult the client’s physiotherapist.

Format
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (Sessions A, B, C) + 2 cardio sessions/week + 1 optional light recovery/core day (Day D).
- Weekly layout (recommended): Mon Strength A, Tue Cardio 1 + light mobility/core, Wed Strength B, Thu Cardio 2, Fri Strength C, Sat Optional Day D or rest, Sun Rest.
- Progression phases:
  - Phase 1 — Foundation: Weeks 1–4 (form, control, moderate loads)
  - Phase 2 — Build (intensified): Weeks 5–8 (increased load, sets, tempo, carries, conditioning)
  - Phase 3 — Strength & Robustness: Weeks 9–12 (heavier submax work, prepare for and perform 1RM tests in Week 12)
- Core work: 2–4 short core blocks/week (10–20 min) focused on anti‑extension and anti‑rotation. Avoid loaded spinal flexion.
- Cardio: 2 low‑impact sessions/week (one interval, one steady) progressed across phases.
- Nutrition: anti‑inflammatory emphasis, protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, omega‑3s, colourful veg, whole foods. Supplements optional per prior guidance.
- Sleep & recovery: target 7–9 h nightly, nightly wind‑down, pre/post workout nutrition, planned deloads, tracking.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: train movement patterns, build posterior chain, single‑leg strength and core stability. RPE 6–7. Main lifts: 3 sets x 8–12 reps (tempo controlled). Cardio: LISS + light intervals.

Weekly template (example)
- Session A — Upper + hip hinge
  - Warm-up 8–12 min
  - Trap‑bar deadlift (light/moderate): 3 x 8
  - Single‑arm cable/seated row: 3 x 10
  - Incline DB press: 3 x 10
  - Single‑leg RDL (DB/KB): 3 x 8 each
  - Pallof press: 3 x 12 each
  - Farmer carry: 2 x 30–45s

- Session B — Lower emphasis, spine‑safe
  - Warm-up
  - Goblet squat to box: 3 x 10
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 each
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust (moderate): 3 x 10
  - Seated/lying hamstring curl: 3 x 12
  - Side plank: 3 x 20–30s / dead bug: 3 x 10 each

- Session C — Upper + posterior chain
  - Warm-up
  - Chest‑supported row: 3 x 10
  - Seated/machine shoulder press: 3 x 10
  - Lat pulldown / pull‑up progression: 3 x 8–10
  - Single‑arm DB bench/floor press: 3 x 8 each
  - Suitcase carry/offset carry: 2 x 30–45s

- Cardio (2x/wk)
  - Cardio 1 (interval light): Bike 5 min warm-up, 6 x 20s hard / 100s easy, 5 min cool-down (20–25 min total)
  - Cardio 2 (steady): Bike/pool/walk 30 min conversational pace

- Core (2–3 short blocks/wk)
  - Dead bug 3 x 8–12, Plank 3 x 20–40s, Pallof 3 x 10 each side, Bird dog 2 x 8 each

Progression across Weeks 2–4
- Add 1–2 reps or small load increases each week when form is solid.
- Week 3 add tempo (3s eccentrics) on selected lifts.
- Week 4 add a set to main lifts if recovery fine (e.g., 4 sets).

Phase 2 — Build / Intensified (Weeks 5–8) — pushed intensity
Goal: increase strength stimulus while respecting spine rules. RPE 7.5–8.5. Main lifts lower reps/higher load, more sets, tempo and pause variations, heavier carries and one controlled metabolic conditioning per week.

Key changes vs Phase 1
- Primary lifts: 4–5 sets x 4–6 reps for trap‑bar, hip thrust, split squats.
- Accessory: 3–4 sets x 6–10.
- Introduce paused reps, tempo eccentrics, cluster sets for heavy accumulation (submax).
- Increase carries: 3 x 40–60s → 60–90s as tolerance allows.
- Add one short EMOM/low‑impact metabolic session per week (10–12 min).

Weekly template (example)
- Session A — Heavy hip hinge emphasis
  - Warm-up
  - Trap‑bar deadlift: 5 x 4–6 (build to RPE ~8)
  - Heavy single‑arm row (chest‑supported option): 4 x 6–8
  - Incline DB press: 4 x 6–8
  - Single‑leg RDL heavier: 3 x 6 each
  - Pallof press (long hold): 3 x 8–10 each
  - Farmer carry heavy: 3 x 60s

- Session B — Unilateral & posterior strength
  - Warm-up
  - Safety‑bar or goblet split squat: 4 x 6 each
  - Barbell hip thrust: 5 x 4–6 (2s pause top on last rep)
  - Leg press heavy: 3 x 8–10
  - Romanian DL (DB): 3 x 8
  - Side plank with leg raise: 3 x 10 each

- Session C — Upper heavy + posterior
  - Warm-up
  - Chest‑supported machine row heavy: 4 x 6
  - Seated DB press: 4 x 6–8
  - Weighted pull‑up / heavy lat pulldown: 4 x 6–8
  - Single‑arm floor press heavy: 3 x 6 each
  - Loaded carries circuit: 3 rounds x 40–60s

- Cardio (2x/wk)
  - Interval day: Bike 5 min warm-up, 8 x 30s hard / 90s easy, 5 min cool-down (25–30 min)
  - Steady day: Bike/elliptical/swim 35–40 min

- Core progressions
  - Plank 3 x 45–60s, Single‑leg RDL 3 x 6–8, Single‑leg Pallof 3 x 8 each, Ab wheel (kneeling) 3 x 6–8 only if pain‑free

Weekly progression (Weeks 5–8)
- Week 5: Implement increases (5–10% load on main lifts vs Phase 1).
- Week 6: Add tempo eccentrics and paused sets; small load bumps (+2.5–5% if previous session RPE ≤7.5).
- Week 7: Cluster or paused higher‑intensity accumulation sets (avoid true max).
- Week 8: Peak phase intensity, then slight volume trim for recovery/taper into Phase 3.

Phase 3 — Strength & Robustness (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: consolidate strength, heavier submax loads, prepare for 1RM testing in Week 12. Avoid maximal loading until test week. RPE 7.5–8.5 on work sets, structured taper before testing.

Weeks 9–10
- Maintain heavy but controlled loading:
  - Trap‑bar deadlift: 4–5 sets x 4–6 (RPE ~8)
  - Barbell hip thrust: 4–5 x 4–6
  - Upper work: 4 x 6, rows and presses heavy
- Cardio: interval session of 6–8 x 30–90s as tolerated; steady session 35–45 min.
- Core: heavier Pallof, loaded carries 3 x 60–90s, advanced anti‑rotation chops (cable) 3 x 8–10.

Week 11 — heavy singles & taper
- Early week: 1–2 heavy singles/doubles at ~90–92% estimated 1RM on trap‑bar and hip thrust (no maximal attempts).
- Mid/late week: technical speed work at 60–70% and mobility; reduce accessory volume ~20–30%.
- Cardio reduced intensity; prioritize sleep and recovery.

Week 12 — Test week (1RM) and deload
- Testing plan (recommended split):
  - Monday (Test Day 1): Trap‑bar deadlift 1RM test with full ramp ladder and strict warm‑up; limit to 2–4 max attempts; small jumps (2.5–5 kg) near top; abort if form breaks or back symptoms occur.
  - Thursday (Test Day 2): Barbell hip thrust 1RM test (same warm‑up and attempt rules).
  - Option to test both same day only if client insists and recovers well (not recommended).
- Post‑test: active recovery, light mobility, LISS, reduced volume for remaining days.
- If testing, follow the warm‑up ladders, autoregulation rules, and safety checklists provided earlier.

Core protocol (summary & progression)
- Frequency: 2–4 short blocks/week, 10–20 min each.
- Focus: anti‑extension (plank, dead bug), anti‑rotation (Pallof press), lateral stability (side plank, carries), dynamic single‑leg control (bird dog, single‑leg RDL).
- Phase progression:
  - Phase 1: dead bug, plank 3 x 20–30s, Pallof 3 x 10, bird dog.
  - Phase 2: plank 3 x 45–60s, single‑leg Pallof 3 x 8–10, carries heavier 3 x 60s, ab wheel (kneeling) only if pain‑free.
  - Phase 3: anti‑rotation chops, cable Pallof single‑leg, loaded carry complexes 3 x 60–90s, short high‑quality rollouts if symptom‑free.
- Avoid loaded spinal flexion (weighted situps, heavy cable crunches).

Cardio summary (2 sessions/week, spine‑safe)
- Cardio session 1 (interval): start Phase 1 with 6 x 20/100s. Progress Phase 2 to 8–10 x 30/90s and Phase 3 to 6–8 x 40/80s at maintained control.
- Cardio session 2 (steady LISS): 30 min Phase 1 → 35–45 min Phase 2–3.
- Modalities: bike, elliptical, pool walking, brisk incline treadmill walking, rowing with shortened stroke — avoid running or high‑impact until cleared.

Anti‑inflammatory nutrition (summary)
- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; calorie maintenance or slight surplus for gains.
- Prioritise: fatty fish (2–3x/wk), olive oil, nuts/seeds (flax/chia), colourful vegetables & berries, legumes, whole grains, turmeric/ginger, collagen (10–20 g/day optional with vitamin C).
- Limit processed foods, refined sugars, excessive omega‑6 oils, and excessive alcohol.
- Supplements optional: fish oil (1–2 g EPA+DHA), vitamin D if low, magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg nightly if needed, curcumin formulation with piperine (check meds).
- Pre/post workout: carb snack pre if needed; post workout 20–40 g protein + carbs within 1–2 hours.

Sleep & recovery protocol (summary)
- Sleep 7–9 h / night; consistent schedule; 60–90 min wind‑down (dim lights, no screens).
- Pre‑bed snack with 20–40 g protein if training later.
- Short naps (10–30 min) before 3 pm if needed.
- Nightly 10–15 min mobility + 5–10 min breathing/meditation.

Which lifts to test (recommended)
- Trap-bar deadlift 1RM — safer axial loading than conventional deadlift, allows neutral spine and torso support.

- Week 12: Test week — two testing days (separated, e.g., Mon and Thu) or both on one day if client prefers and recovery allows. Detailed week-by-week adjustments

Week 10 (preparation)
- Reduce overall accessory volume by ~10–15% versus intensified Phase 2 weeks.
- Focus on technical work and speed-strength:
  - Trap-bar: 4 sets x 3 reps at ~75–80% of estimated 1RM, focusing on speed and perfect mechanics.
  - Hip thrust: 4 x 3 at ~75–80% focusing on full hip extension and control.
- Continue upper/lower program but reduce total accessory sets; keep core and carries but moderate load/duration.
- Continue cardio as usual but reduce interval intensity slightly if fatigue appears.

Week 11 (heavy singles & taper)
- Purpose: expose CNS to heavy loads near 1RM but avoid true maximal efforts; decrease volume so client will be fresh for Week 12.
- Session early week (e.g., Mon or Tue):
  - Trap-bar: work up to heavy single/double at ~90–92% estimated 1RM (no max), total of 1–2 heavy singles only. Warm-up ladder as below.
  - Hip thrust: work up to heavy double at ~88–92% estimated 1RM.
- Mid-week: light technique session (e.g., speed trap-bar 3 x 2 at 60–70%, hip thrust 3 x 3 at 60–70), mobility, sleep focus.
- Late-week: rest or very light session. Avoid heavy conditioning 48–72 hours before test.

Week 12 (test week) — structure
- Option A (recommended): Split testing across two days to minimize fatigue:
  - Day 1 (e.g., Monday): Trap-bar deadlift 1RM test.
  - Day 2 (e.g., Thursday): Barbell hip thrust 1RM test.
  - This allows 48–72 hours recovery and better performance.
- Option B: Single-day testing (if client insists) — test trap-bar first, rest 3–4 hours, then hip thrust second. Less ideal.

General testing safety & rules (must follow strictly)
- Medical/physio clearance confirmed and client is asymptomatic that day.
- Good sleep (7–9 hours) the night before testing day and normal nutrition/hydration.
- No heavy lower-body training 5–7 days before test beyond the planned Week 11 submax exposures.
- Warm-up thoroughly with progressive ramp sets (detailed below).
- Use a spotter/assistant for hip thrust (for safety getting into/out of position and for loading/unloading).
- Maintain bracing technique on all attempts; avoid breath-holding for prolonged Valsalva — employ braced exhale technique.
- Abort test if any low-back pain, radicular signs, or unusual neurologic symptoms occur.
- Aim for true 1RM but keep subjectively safe — stop if RPE >9.5 or form breaks.

Warm-up ladders and attempt progression (example)
- General warm-up: 8–12 minutes of easy bike/row, dynamic t-spine mobility, glute activation and 2–3 ramp sets of the movement pattern with empty/small load.
- Specific ramp ladder for trap-bar deadlift (example):
  - Bar only (or light trap-bar): 8–10 reps
  - 40% estimated 1RM: 5 reps
  - 55%: 3 reps
  - 70%: 2 reps
  - 80%: 1 rep
  - 90%: 1 rep
  - Then attempt 1RM (add 2.5–5 kg increments; rest 3–5 minutes between heavy singles)
- Specific ramp for hip thrust:
  - Bodyweight glute bridge: 8–10 reps
  - Bar only: 8–10 reps
  - 40% est. 1RM: 5 reps
  - 60%: 3 reps
  - 75%: 2 reps
  - 85–90%: 1 rep
  - Then attempt 1RM (small jumps 2.5–5 kg). Rest 3–5 minutes between maximal attempts.

Autoregulation and attempt strategy
- Use RPE and bar speed as guides. If a heavy single at a planned load feels slow and RPE ≥9.5 or form degrades, do not increase load.
- Limit total maximal attempts to reduce spinal stress: aim for 2–4 maximal singles per lift (including the one that becomes the PR). If client feels strong after one successful attempt, add a conservative jump; if not, stop.
- Prefer smaller increment jumps (2.5–5 kg) near the top to reduce risk.
- If any attempt shows form breakdown (lumbar rounding, hinge moving into flexion, jerky movement), stop and do not attempt higher.

Post-test protocol (same day)
- Light cool-down: 5–10 min very easy bike; light mobility and glute activation.
- Gentle posterior chain stretching and foam rolling (avoid aggressive spinal manipulation).
- Protein + carbohydrate meal within 1–2 hours (25–40 g protein) to support recovery.
- Prioritise sleep and hydration that night.

Post-test week (Week 12 remainder)
- Active recovery/deload for the rest of the week: keep sessions light — 50–60% of usual loads, reduced volume (40–60% of sets). Focus on mobility, core stability, and low-impact cardio (LISS).
- Avoid max or near-max attempts for the next 7–10 days while tissues and CNS recover.

Example micro-schedule for Week 12 (split testing)

  - Warm-up ladder, 1–3 attempts to find 1RM, finish with easy glute activation and light cool-down.
- Tuesday — Recovery: mobility, light walk or bike 20–30 min, core breath work.
- Wednesday — Light full-body session (low volume): 2 sets of main movements at ~50–60% with technical focus; core and carries light.

Notes on data and progression after testing
- Record 1RM values, RPE, technique notes and any symptoms.
- Use 1RM to re-calculate training percentages for next cycle, but consider autoregulation and back history — avoid programming frequent heavy singles or loads above ~90% for prolonged periods.
- Consider moving to a hypertrophy/strength blend or deload phase after testing to consolidate gains safely.

Below is a practical, evidence-informed sleep and recovery protocol you can give your client alongside the 12‑week training, cardio and anti‑inflammatory nutrition plan. It’s tailored for a 42‑year‑old desk worker recovering from an L4–L5 herniation (now asymptomatic) who is training at moderate–high intensity and planning 1RM testing in Week 12. Focus is on improving sleep quality, accelerating tissue repair, reducing inflammation, and managing fatigue so he can train hard while staying safe.

Quick summary
- Target sleep: 7–9 hours per night, consistent schedule.
- Priorities: regular sleep timing, pre‑sleep routine, nutrition and hydration that support recovery, movement/daytime activity, strategic napping, monitored load & planned deloads, and simple recovery modalities (mobility, soft tissue, cold/heat as needed).
- Track: daily sleep hours + sleep quality (1–5), training RPE, soreness, and any back symptoms. Adjust training if sleep or recovery metrics decline.

1) Sleep targets and timing
- Aim for 7–9 hours nightly. For most men 42 y/o, 7.5–8.5 is a good target.
- Keep sleep/wake times consistent (±30 minutes). Anchor wake time (easier than bed time) and shift bedtime to ensure total sleep.
- Prioritise earlier sleep onset rather than late nights — hormonal recovery (growth hormone, testosterone) and inflammatory markers benefit from consolidated night sleep.

2) Pre-sleep routine (60–90 min wind‑down)
- Fixed wind‑down window nightly (e.g., 9:30–10:30 pm if target sleep 11 pm).
- Light: dim overhead lighting 60–90 minutes before bed. Avoid bright screens or use blue‑light filters.
- Activities: low‑stimulus activities — reading, gentle stretching, mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, brief meditation (5–10 min).
- Temperature: keep bedroom cool (18–20°C / 64–68°F) for better sleep onset and quality.
- Caffeine cut-off: avoid caffeine 6–8 hours before bedtime. For a 42‑year‑old, 6 hours is a reasonable minimum.
- Alcohol: keep to a minimum; avoid within 3–4 hours of bedtime. Alcohol fragments sleep architecture and impairs recovery.
- Light snack: if hungry before bed, a small protein + carbohydrate snack (e.g., Greek yogurt + berries) is fine; avoid heavy meals within 1–2 hours of bed.

3) Sleep hygiene & environment
- Mattress/pillow: ensure lumbar-friendly support. Pillow height and mattress firmness should keep spine neutral while sleeping.
- Reduce noise/light: blackout curtains, white noise machine if needed.
- Keep bedroom for sleep (and intimacy) only — avoid working in bed to strengthen sleep cueing.

4) Napping strategy
- Short naps (10–30 minutes) can be useful for daytime alertness and recovery but keep naps before 3 pm to avoid interfering with night sleep.
- Avoid long naps (>60 min) late in day which can reduce night sleep drive.

5) Nutrition & timing for recovery
- Protein before bed: 20–40 g casein‑rich protein or mixed protein (e.g., cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, or a slow‑release protein) can support overnight muscle protein synthesis and recovery.
- Evening carbs: a moderate amount post-evening training supports glycogen and sleep (e.g., rice + lean protein), but avoid heavy late meals.
- Hydration: maintain hydration across the day; avoid excess fluids within 60–90 min of bed to reduce nocturnal awakenings.
- Supplements to consider (with GP/clinician approval): magnesium (glycinate) 200–400 mg in the evening for sleep and muscle relaxation; low-dose melatonin (0.5–2 mg) short-term for circadian realignment only if needed; vitamin D if deficient; avoid excessive stimulants in evening.

6) Recovery scheduling and load management
- Planned micro‑deloads: built into the program — Week 11 is a taper; Week 12 post‑testing is a deload. Use objective markers to adjust:
  - If sleep quality drops for 3+ nights or RPE/soreness increases notably, reduce volume by ~20–30% for 3–7 days.
- Training timing: schedule heavy sessions earlier in the day when possible. Late night heavy sessions may impair sleep onset.
- Cardio: schedule interval sessions earlier; steady-state cardio can be later but not directly before bed.

7) Daily and post‑session recovery practices
- Immediate post‑session:
  - Cool‑down 5–10 minutes light movement (bike or walk), followed by mobility for hips/thoracic spine and gentle stretching of hamstrings/glutes.
  - Post‑session nutrition: 20–40 g protein with some carbs within 1–2 hours.
- Evening mobility: 10–15 minutes of thoracic mobility, hip flexor release, glute activation and gentle hamstring work to reduce stiffness from desk job and training load.
- Self‑myofascial release: foam rolling 5–10 minutes for glutes, hamstrings, lats as needed — avoid aggressive lumbar rolling. Use lacrosse ball on glute med/min cautiously.
- Cold/heat: brief cold for acute inflammation (if any new flare); heat and light massage for chronic tightness. Use whichever feels best for muscle soreness — e.g., 10–15 min contrast shower or 10–20 min heat pack for tightness.
- Compression garments: optional for long day of standing or travel; modest benefit for perceived recovery.

8) Stress, autonomic recovery & breathing
- Daily breathing practice: 5–10 minutes diaphragmatic breathing or box breathing in the evening to activate parasympathetic tone and improve sleep onset.
- Mindfulness/meditation: 5–10 minutes before bed or after evening mobility reduces cortisol and aids sleep.
- Light exposure: get 10–30 minutes morning sunlight exposure to entrain circadian rhythm and improve sleep onset at night.

9) Monitoring and objective metrics
- Simple tracking: daily log of:
  - Sleep start/stop time and total hours,
  - Sleep quality rating (1–5),
  - Training RPE and readiness (1–5),
  - Low‑back pain or other symptoms (yes/no and severity).
- If possible, use wearable or apps to track sleep duration and consistency (actigraphy is a useful adjunct). But subjective sleep quality matters most; use both.
- Use scores to adjust training: e.g., if sleep <6.5 h two nights in a row and readiness low, shift that day’s session to light/moderate or reduce load.

10) Recovery week & 1RM testing considerations
- In the 7–10 days around 1RM testing:
  - Prioritise sleep and avoid travel or heavy late nights.
  - Keep alcohol to a minimum and ensure good night sleep before test day.
  - Use Week 11 taper to lower volume and allow stronger sleep–recovery.
- Post‑test: use a 3–7 day lighter phase focusing on mobility, low-impact cardio, and reduced volume to allow CNS and tissue recovery.

11) Red flags and when to consult the physio/MD
- Increasing nighttime pain, radicular symptoms (numbness/tingling), or new neurological signs.
- Significant or prolonged sleep disruption despite following protocol — refer for sleep medicine assessment if suspected sleep apnea or chronic insomnia.
- Unexplained worsening of pain with training even after reducing load.

Practical checklist to give the client
- Fixed wake time within 30 minutes daily.
- Wind‑down routine starts 60–90 minutes before bed (dim lights, no screens).
- 7–9 hours sleep target; track duration and quality nightly.
- Pre‑bed snack: 20–40 g protein if training later or to support overnight recovery.
- Short nap (10–30 min) if needed, before 3 pm.
- Nightly 10–15 min mobility + 5–10 min breathing/meditation.
- Record sleep + RPE + soreness daily and adjust training if needed.

- Frequency: 2–4 short blocks/week, 10–20 min each.

- Keep a training log: loads, sets, RPE, carry times/distances, cardio HR/RPE, sleep hours/quality, and any back symptoms. Review weekly and adjust.
